key_insight: WEST is a scalable open-source platform for excited-state simulations that combines GW, BSE, TDDFT, and embedding methods without explicit virtual states, enabling large-system accuracy on modern HPC hardware.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar-cell research, WEST can model optical spectra, self-trapped excitons, and excited-state processes at realistic system sizes, helping connect atomistic physics to device-relevant performance.
method: Full-frequency GW, Bethe-Salpeter equation, TDDFT, and quantum defect embedding in one framework
Avoids explicit virtual-state calculation using density-functional and density-matrix perturbation theory
Uses low-rank dielectric/exchange representations, localization, hierarchical parallelism, and GPU acceleration
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong scaling to thousands of GPUs and successful applications to systems with more than a thousand atoms, including self-trapped excitons in metal-halide perovskites.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy depend on advanced HPC resources and careful workflow integration across multiple coupled methods.
paper_title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
